qs.q: A patient with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency develops hemolytic anemia after taking an oxidant drug. Why does this enzyme deficiency cause red blood cell lysis?
o: Inability to generate sufficient ATP for membrane ion pumps
Defected synthesis of membrane cholesterol and phospholipid
Accumulation of toxic glycolitic intermediates in the cytoplasm
Failure to maintain adequate reduced glutathione levels via NADPH
Rapid deplection of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate leading to rigidity
qs.e: G6PD deficiency impairs NADPH production, which is required by glutathione reductase to neutralize oxidative stress in erythrocytes.
qs.s: Weekly Year 1: Carbohydrate Metabolism and Bioenergetics Exam - November 13, 202

qs.q: A patient with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency receives packed red blood cells that have reached their expiration date limit. What specific storage-related phenomenon increases the risk of adverse outcomes?
o: Extracellular potassium accumulation within the storage bag
Progressive degradation of labile coagulation factors
Depletion of intracellular adenosine triphosphate within cells
Bacterial proliferation due to ambient storage temperature
Formation of microaggregates composed of degenerated platelets
qs.e: Prolonged storage leads to red cell membrane breakdown, causing significant extracellular potassium leakage that can affect vulnerable patients.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Blood Transfusion Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)
